title: Round 4, stream B: the chain explained, the antenna on screen and the drop eight days on, the companions out of the tank's way, on DAY 42's dance floor and in the final frame
context: The owner's playtest of b9434246 (2026-11-02), notes 2, 4, 5, 8 and 14 (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-round-4-fifteen-notes-design.md, stream B): 2) "Keep the chain going" explained by Isao with believable technobabble and written in the bestiary; 4) the Ridgeback drop comes too early after the K9 print: a skippable antenna build close-up, Isao says reinforcements come in 8 days, the drop 8 days later; 5) the companions must get out of the tank's way (actively run from a moving hull) instead of being driven through when they come to investigate; 8) DAY 42: camera highlights of the K9 and the feline on the dance floor; 14) the final scene's frame has the K9 and the feline too. Branch round-4-story from overnight-2026-10-23 d05b2a99.
decision: 2) The chain is the kill streak: the trickle's recorded "Keep the chain going." rides the SOFT ONES — KEEP THE CHAIN callout and nothing said what the chain was; the lore was asked at x1.5 and is once per browser. Now chain_lore (renamed from streak_lore so the owner's browser, which may have seen the old beat, hears the new one) is wanted at the first STREAK callout (streak 5), three lines under the panel's 7 s ceiling: 'When they die close together, their membranes cross-link before they break down. A lattice.' / 'The lattice holds the biomass up on the surface, where the treads can scoop it.' / 'One alone just liquefies and seeps into the rock. Keep the chain going.' The bestiary: a fourth Isao line on IVORY and LEMON and a BIOMASS · THE CHAIN note (CHAIN_NOTE, entries flagged chain, entryCard lore, full readings only). 4) REINFORCEMENTS.days 3 -> 8; build_radar's second line 'Printing the antenna. Once it stands I can call for reinforcements. Eight days out.' and reinforcements_called '... eight days to fall.' read the knob (daysWord). The radar step carries closeup: 'antenna': its line waits for the print, src/fx/antenna-print.js asks for it and cuts to the rising structure (ANTENNA_CLOSEUP: four angles over 12 s + 1.5 s, 5 s mandatory, then Space, the hint, the near plane lowered; never over a seat or a shot or with under half the print left). The four-angle rail moved out of pet-print into src/fx/print-closeup.js, used by both. 5) A dodge mode: a hull moving (>0.5 m/s) and closing (>0.3 m/s) within 6 m, or within 60 m and 5 m of its line and due inside 3 s, sends the unit off the line at top speed until it is past, still or 12 m off; it pre-empts everything but the dance; the greet waits for a hull still for 1 s and breaks off as it moves. The host derives the hull's velocity from its point frame to frame. 8) A dance mode while the party is on (tricks, sits and short dashes on a floor 5-13 m from the ball's foot, 9 m off the hull); the reveal cut grows to 6 + 4 s per printed companion (14 s with both), a close shot on C-07 then RECKON K9 with the near plane lowered. 14) The diorama stages a sitting copy of each printed companion beside the hull, in the shot's frame.
outcome: Commits on round-4-story: 70234e00 (note 2), 38dedb5e (note 5), f6b82878 (note 4), 86ec5b48 (notes 8 and 14), bb60d324 (the close shots look past the parked hull), then the records. Measured: the pure drive-at test, closest approach of a hull driven straight at a sitting unit at 6/12/20/30 m/s 11.3/6.7/6.7/5.8 m (C-07) and 9.9/6.6/7.8/4.3 m (K9); in the browser the hull aimed at C-07 27 m off and driven at 99-136 km/h came no closer than 5.2 m (4.7 m on the final run). The antenna cut 13.5 s, four angles. DAY 42: the cut 14 s, each companion 4 m from the lens in its segment; the first frames had the parked hull filling C-07's shot, so each close shot takes the quarter round its companion whose line of sight passes farthest from the hull, and the floor keeps 9 m off it. The finale: hull, C-07 and K9 inside the screen at both ends of the rail (NDC within +-0.7). td-tab 5,353 -> 5,355 (+2). Spec disagreements: the drive-at margin is 4 m, not 2 m (the 10 m hull's half width); the finale's 20 s replay takes no highlights (the boards' shot is the owner's frame, and the companions are staged in it); the antenna browser step replays the standing radar's print (antennaPrint()) because a skip=defence base is static and never prints the radar; the real path is sector 2's step, which --grow drives. Lines are captions until recorded.
alternatives: Keep the lore at x1.5: the owner had not heard it; the first STREAK callout is the earliest moment the chain exists on screen.
Run directly away from the hull: a tank at 30 m/s runs a 7 m/s cat down; leaving the hull's line (the roam cell farthest from it within 25 m) clears it in about a second.
Highlights in the finale's replay too: they would cut away from the boards the owner asked to see; staging the companions in that frame answers note 14 for both.
A forced-print harness through Isao's order book: it would replay the programme's finish and the call; the antenna module replays the print itself (story.print.progress) under the cut instead.
evidence: npm test (312 programs), npm run check, npm run architecture green at each commit; test/tdcore.mjs, test/bestiary.mjs, test/brief-queue.mjs, test/companions.mjs (the drive-at, the greet, the dance), test/antenna-print.mjs (new), test/pet-print.mjs, test/reinforcements.mjs (the spoken wait tied to the knob), test/disco-party.mjs, test/ending-host.mjs.

--companions PASS with the new drive-at check (artifacts/browser/companions-dodge.png); --antenna-print (new) PASS (artifacts/browser/antenna-print-1..4.png); --pet-print PASS on the shared rail; --day-42 with ?pets=born PASS (artifacts/browser/day-42-c07.png, day-42-k9.png); --finale with ?pets=born PASS (artifacts/browser/finale-pets.png).

Final runs on the stream's tree: --companions, --pet-print, --antenna-print, --day-42 (twice, the second after the quarter fix), --finale, --reinforcements-timer and --debrief all PASS; the full default suite's result is in docs/STATE.md's stream B paragraph and the stream's report.
